queries.query: what stops two copies of the background service from both writing to the same index at once
queries.why: This module is the cross-process admission primitive: an exclusive OS lock held for process lifetime, explicitly contrasted with an existence-check lockfile.

queries.query: if a branch switch touches thousands of files at once, how does the tool keep memory from growing without bound
queries.why: queue.rs is a set (not a channel) with a pending-path bound that degrades to a full rescan; watch.rs bounds the callback boundary with a try_send channel plus an overflow bit answered by a rescan.

queries.query: why does compiler output and downloaded package content never turn up in results
queries.why: The single 'is this file indexable' decision point, with a hard-exclude list (target, node_modules, Library, Temp, obj, bin) plus gitignore rules via the ignore crate.

queries.query: how does it tell that a file's contents really changed rather than just its modification time being bumped
queries.why: The indexer's change detection is content hashing rather than mtime, with the reasoning about mtime lying across branch switches and restores stated in the module header and implemented in index_file.

queries.query: what keeps a rough working note from outranking a ratified document when both discuss the same topic
queries.why: Computes the effective tier used by ranking: path ceilings demote scratch and research material, and a 'decided' declaration is honored only if it cites an active ledger entry. The two design docs state the same policy (status-aware ranking) and are accepted alternates.

queries.query: how are two separately ordered result lists combined into one ordering without comparing their raw scores
queries.why: fuse_detailed combines ranks (not magnitudes) from the two arms; the module header explains why blending incomparable BM25 and cosine numbers was rejected.

queries.query: if the server replies with the batch shuffled, how does each vector still land on the snippet it belongs to
queries.why: restore_order rebuilds input order from each response item's index field and validates widths, calling a misattached vector a silent permanent corruption.

queries.query: how does an editor plugin figure out where to reach the local service after it has been restarted on a new port
queries.why: lore-mcp re-reads the discovery record on every tool call precisely because the process it proxies restarts with a new port and pid; lore-core owns the record type, its freshness rule and data-directory resolution.

queries.query: when an agent asks to see more of the surrounding lines, is that text read fresh from the file or served from what was stored
queries.why: States outright that the text comes from disk rather than the index, and that the stored chunk is only a fallback when disk and index disagree.

queries.query: what happens if someone types unbalanced quotes or stray brackets into the search box
queries.why: sanitize_fts_query whitelists alphanumeric runs into quoted phrase terms so unterminated quotes, stray parens and bare operators can never produce a syntax error.

queries.query: does search degrade to lexical-only when the embedding endpoint is missing or unhealthy
queries.why: The embed module header states the D-0007 contract directly: absent or unhealthy endpoint degrades search to lexical-only, visibly in GET /v1/status, and never fails a search.

queries.query: how large can a chunk be before it is split into overlapping windows, and what are the chunk size limits
queries.why: Defines MAX_FILE_BYTES, MAX_CHUNK_BYTES, TINY_CHUNK_BYTES, SMALL_CONTAINER_BYTES, TEXT_WINDOW_LINES and WINDOW_OVERLAP_LINES with the rationale for each.

queries.query: which FTS5 tokenizer does the SQLite schema use and why is underscore a token character
queries.why: The migration doc explains the unicode61 remove_diacritics 2 tokenchars '_' choice and why stock unicode61 shatters snake_case identifiers.

queries.query: how does the watcher handle nested project roots where one registered root contains another
queries.why: The pump routes each event to all roots containing it; routing to the first match is named as the defect that leaves the other project's index permanently stale.

queries.query: what is the retry policy, backoff delay and request timeout for embedding requests
queries.why: DEFAULT_MAX_ATTEMPTS, RETRY_BASE_DELAY, RETRY_MAX_DELAY and REQUEST_TIMEOUT are declared here with their rationale.

queries.query: where is bare_supersedes_list defined
queries.why: The function is defined here; it is also the canonical source cited by decision D-0010.

queries.query: which file contains the sanitize_fts_query function
queries.why: sanitize_fts_query is declared in this module.

queries.query: where does page_is_final live
queries.why: page_is_final is defined here as the acquisition loop's stop condition.

queries.query: where is Store::apply_project_set implemented
queries.why: The method and its remove/release/claim ordering are implemented on Store in this file.

queries.query: why did we decide to build a new context daemon instead of adopting or forking an existing one
queries.why: D-0002 records the accepted decision to build Lore, with the rationale that the commodity layer is solved everywhere while the motivating capabilities exist nowhere.

queries.query: what is the authority order in this vault and how does a document become canon
queries.why: Lists the six-level authority order, the design_status document states, the certainty callouts, and the promotion rules that gate canon.

queries.query: what does the design say the ranking steps must be and which part is a requirement versus tuning
queries.why: The Ranking section specifies BM25 plus vector cosine fused with RRF, then a vault-status modifier after fusion, and states that the ordering is the requirement while weights are tuning.

queries.query: what ships in each milestone and what is on the backlog
queries.why: Enumerates M0 through M4, the indexing scope note, the backlog items, and the benchmark posture.

queries.query: which tools are in the v0.1 MCP surface and what was deliberately excluded from it
queries.why: Names search, expand and status as the v0.1 tools and lists the deliberate exclusions (registration/reindex are CLI-only, no memory-write API, no graph tools).

queries.query: what did the post-mortem conclude about the earlier tool that made the machine unusable
queries.why: The CCE post-mortem section walks the five findings (process-local asyncio locks, per-process watchers, mutual re-indexing cascade, stale lifecycle state, the 36-indexer issue) and the resulting design lessons.
